question: In which state is 'Bhogali Bihu' festival celebrated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhogali Bihu** is one of the most important festivals celebrated in the state of **Assam**.
 
• Also known as **Magh Bihu**, it marks the end of the harvesting season in the month of **Magh** (January-February).
 
• The festival is characterized by **community feasts**, bonfires, and the preparation of traditional Assamese delicacies.
 
• It is a time for farmers to relax and enjoy the fruits of their labor with family and friends.
 
• Various traditional games like **tekeli bhonga** (pot-breaking) and **buffalo fighting** are organized during the celebrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bihu Festival**

 
 
• There are three main types of Bihu celebrated in Assam: **Bohag Bihu** (Rongali Bihu), **Kati Bihu** (Kongali Bihu), and **Magh Bihu** (Bhogali Bihu).
 
• Bohag Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and the arrival of spring.
 
• Kati Bihu is observed in the month of Kati (October) and is associated with the relocation of crops and the lighting of lamps.
 
• Magh Bihu, as mentioned, celebrates the end of the harvest season.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Foods**
 
 
• During Bhogali Bihu, people prepare various traditional dishes such as **pitha** (rice cakes), **laru** (coconut and sesame sweets), and **doi** (curd).
 
• Community feasts called **bhog** are organized where neighbors and relatives come together to share food.
 
 
 
• **Meji and Bhela Ghar**
 
 
• **Meji** is a bonfire made of wood and bamboo, symbolizing the end of the harvesting period.
 
• **Bhela Ghar** are temporary huts made from bamboo, leaves, and thatch, where people gather to eat and celebrate.
 
• These structures are usually burnt at the end of the festival as part of the ritual.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance**
 
 
• The festival fosters a sense of community and reinforces cultural bonds among the Assamese people.
 
• It also reflects the agrarian lifestyle of Assam, highlighting the importance of agriculture in the region.
